about: Cases for binning small models (TASK-104). Every case runs with skills on and skills off. 'tool' is the skill a case needs with skills on (null: none; 'optional': either). 'checks' grade the final reply; 'off' says what counts as right with skills off: 'same' (the checks), 'honest' (says it cannot know or check, and does not invent), or 'value' (the checks, as the model can work it out itself). 'rubric' cases are also read by a person.

filler: Here is some background for a report I am writing about community gardens. Many towns have turned unused plots into shared gardens, where neighbours grow vegetables, herbs and flowers side by side. The gardens are usually run by volunteers, who set the rules for watering, composting and sharing tools.

Most gardens split the land into small beds, one for each household, with a few shared beds for fruit bushes and herbs. Waiting lists are common in cities, and some gardens give priority to people without a garden of their own.

Funding tends to come from small grants, plot fees and plant sales. The biggest costs are water, fencing and tools, and in some places insurance. A few gardens run workshops on pruning, seed saving and pest control to raise money.

Volunteers say the social side matters as much as the food. Older members pass on skills to newer ones, children learn where food comes from, and people who would not otherwise meet end up sharing seedlings and recipes.

The main problems reported are theft, vandalism and disputes over neglected beds. Most gardens deal with these through clear written rules, a small committee and regular work days when everyone tidies the shared areas together.
